preamble: An open vowel that raises step by step and ends up as a front diphthong [eɪ]. The standard case is the English Great Vowel Shift. Middle English long /aː/ (in name, make, face) moved through [æː], [ɛː] and [eː] and diphthongized to [eɪ] around 1800. Northern English and Scottish accents kept a monophthong [eː]. A clear second case from another language has not been found, so the change from a to ei is treated as rare.

examples.note: Great Vowel Shift chain aː > æː > ɛː > eː > eɪ; the final diphthongization dates to about 1800, and northern English and Scottish accents keep monophthongal [eː].

sources: Wikipedia (2026). Phonological history of English diphthongs. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonological_history_of_English_diphthongs
Labov, W. (1994). Principles of Linguistic Change, Volume I: Internal Factors. Oxford: Blackwell.
